errors.english: Then, having understood that this is difficult to find, the Blessed One spoke to the retinue, who had become faithful and inspired
errors.why: It is the retinue who, through faith, understood that this is hard to find and became enthusiastic; the English makes the Blessed One the one who understood.

note: Verses on the cakras and the two stages and the opening commentary are rendered faithfully; one dangling participle shifts who understood.

errors.english: so too is the aspect non-distinct from the manifestation
errors.why: The Tibetan says that likewise the aspect, being non-distinct from the manifestations, is also diverse; the English turns the predicate into a claim of non-distinctness.

note: A dense Pramāṇa commentary followed closely and mostly correctly; awkward doubled glosses but the argument is preserved.

errors.english: The syllable (ba) part of the cry of lamentation is the sound of (kyema) alas/how tragic.
errors.why: བ completes རྗེས་སུ་བརྩེ་བ from the previous side: 'kye ma is the word used for one to be pitied'; there is no syllable 'ba' or cry of lamentation.

errors.english: It should be understood as "The practitioner spoke in this way."
errors.why: The construal is 'spoke such mantras' (the commentary then glosses mantra), i.e. the deities uttered the mantra, not 'the practitioner spoke'.

note: The mantra glosses are largely right, but the opening misreads a boundary word and the speaker of the mantra is shifted to the practitioner.

errors.english: as it is from these that one must emerge from afflictive emotions
errors.why: The worldly is the three realms because it proceeds into (ལ) the afflictions, in contrast to the transcendent which emerges from (ལས) them; the English gives the worldly the definition of the transcendent.

note: A generally sound rendering of the practice commentary; the worldly/transcendent contrast is blurred.

errors.english: elders, and women with your servants and retinues
errors.why: The list is old men and old women (with servants and retinue); 'old' is dropped from the women.

note: The vajra-gaze, expulsion formula and vajra-gait are rendered accurately; the closing verse is put as prose but its sense is kept.

errors.english: "Lord, given that no phenomenon is apprehended when they have stood in suchness and practiced for suchness, how will they stand in the knowledge of all aspects?"
errors.why: The Tibetan cites only the abbreviated lemma 'Lord, having stood in suchness and applied themselves to suchness'; the rest of the question is supplied from the sūtra without marking.

errors.english: "Lord, given that no dharma called 'a tathāgata's magical creation' is apprehended at all, who will stand in suchness?"
errors.why: The Tibetan has only 'that which is called a tathāgata's emanation'; the non-apprehension clause and the question are added.

errors.english: teach the Dharma in the form of a proclamation of the names
errors.why: The buddhas proclaim the bodhisattvas' names and teach the Dharma joyfully (in a manner of delight); 'joyfully' is not rendered.

note: The list of questions is correctly numbered and mostly accurate, but two abbreviated lemmas are silently completed from the sūtra.

errors.english: If a Buddha or a Bodhisattva who practices the supreme conduct of mantra is exhorted according to the described method
errors.why: The buddha or bodhisattva is the one urged by the practitioner of the supreme mantra conduct, and it is the deity who would transgress the samaya if the rite fails; the English merges exhorter and exhorted.

errors.english: If the practitioner does not enter into the sequence exactly as it is described, they should, in short, begin the fierce practice upon seeing the result
errors.why: The ergative སྒྲུབ་པ་པོས་ marks the practitioner as the one who undertakes the fierce rite; the one who does not engage in the stated order is the deity being urged.

note: The yogic glosses are rendered understandably, but the argument about who is urged and who transgresses is confused.

errors.english: In my tradition, the results produced by self-reproach, full confession, and so forth, are either diminished by some means or exhausted by opportunity. However, they are not exhausted by something produced by a different, discordant category.
errors.why: Self-reproach, confession etc. are the means by which the result produced by a given action is diminished or exhausted, while a result produced by another action of a discordant kind is not; the English makes them the producers of the results and inverts the second clause.

fix.find: In my tradition, the results produced by self-reproach, full confession, and so forth, are either diminished by some means or exhausted by opportunity. However, they are not exhausted by something produced by a different, discordant category.
fix.replace: In my tradition, through some means such as self-reproach, full confession, and so forth, the result produced [by an action] becomes small or, as the occasion arises, is exhausted; but a result produced by another action of a discordant kind is not.

errors.english: If one wonders, "How is it that by the very experience of the result of sinful deeds, the results of merit are also exhausted?"
errors.why: The commented lemma 'mixed capacities' (ནུས་འདྲེས) that this sentence explains is not translated.

note: The karma-exhaustion argument is mostly followed, but the key statement of the author's own position confuses means and results.

errors.english: May I give rise to all those miraculous powers.
errors.why: འཚལ་བ here means to know (Skt. prajāne): 'may I know all their manifestations', not 'give rise to'.

note: A good rendering of the Bhadracarī verses; one verb is misread.

errors.english: "I shall pay homage to this as a stupa"
errors.why: འཚལ་བར་བགྱི means 'I shall regard/know (it) as', not 'pay homage'; the same misreading recurs for the Tathāgatas and Vajrapāṇi, which obscures the commentary's point that the text is to be regarded as a relic-stupa.

fix.find: "I shall pay homage to this as a stupa"
fix.replace: "I shall regard this as a stupa"

errors.english: King of Tantras [note: the Hevajra Tantra]
errors.why: The scene (Vajrapāṇi exhorting Brahmā, Indra and the gods to protect practitioners) is not the Hevajra; the note misidentifies the kalparāja being commented on.

note: The exhortation passage reads well, but the recurring 'pay homage' for འཚལ་བར་བགྱི and a wrong identifying note need correction; a stray 'continues to next page' remains.
